# US Consumer Sentiment Improves in November

The University of Michigan’s consumer sentiment index rose to 51.0 in early November 2026, up from 48.0 in October and comfortably above market expectations of 48.0.

Modest gains across several components, including expectations for personal finances and business conditions, were driven primarily by independent voters. [...] Sentiment improved among lower- and middle-wealth households but fell 5% among consumers with the largest stock portfolios, following a relatively turbulent period in equity markets.

Economists generally assess a measure known as "core" CPI — which strips out volatile food and energy prices — to examine underlying inflation dynamics in the U.S. economy.

That core metric rose 0.3% in October, as it also did in September and August. A consistent monthly reading around 0.2% would be more in line with the Fed's 2% annual inflation target, Zandi said.

Inflation has been above the Fed's target for more than five years.
